 | 6:06 PM MYT

 KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) today issued a policy document that establishes a regulatory framework for open finance to facilitate consent-driven sharing of customer information across the financial sector in a secure, open, accessible, interoperable and timely manner.
 In a statement, the central bank outlined several requirements and expectations, including the scope of participation and customer information to be shared, as well as implementation timelines for mandated participation and sharing of customer information.
 It also sets out requirements for managing customer consent, including the obtaining, monitoring, renewal and revocation of consent, alongside safeguards and controls for protecting customer information.
 The framework also addresses the management of technology and cybersecurity risks associated with open finance.
 "Open finance gives customers greater control over how their financial information is shared through clear consent parameters, supported by a more secure and standardised framework for data-sharing. 
 "BNM will continue to set out clear regulatory requirements to ensure such sharing remains safe and responsible," it said.
 The BNM open finance policy document is available on the central bank’s website. - Bernama
